title: Composition isomorphism for $Lf^*$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$
statement:
For morphisms $f\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to Z$ of the setting and a commutative condensed
ring $\Lambda$, the *composition isomorphism*

$$
L(g\circ f)^*\cong Lf^*\circ Lg^*\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)
$$

of the restricted pullbacks of [def-sfb-dc-upper-star] is the unique natural isomorphism whose
image under the inclusion into $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ is the ambient composition isomorphism.

proof.text: For each $h=f,g,g\circ f$, [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main] gives that the underived module-object pullback $h^*$ is additive and exact. The derived pullback $L_h$ of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] is the total left derived functor of $h^*$ computed on K-flat resolutions, so the existence hypotheses of the left-derived clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] are in force; by its exact-functor clause $L_h$ is identified with the termwise functor $D(h^*)$. Since $h^*$ is exact, $\operatorname{CoCh}(h^*)$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so the localized termwise functor inverts them.

Let $a:(g\circ f)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}f^*g^*$ be [def-sfb-module-upper-star-comp]. The node [prop-sfb-module-left-derived-upper-star-comp] gives the ambient comparison $c:L_{g\circ f}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_fL_g$ induced by $a$. Explicitly, if $Q_S$ denotes the derived localization and $\psi_h:L_hQ_S\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_T\operatorname{CoCh}(h^*)$ is the exact-functor comparison, then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] descends the degreewise chain isomorphism $a_{K^n}$ to the unique transformation with $c_{Q_ZK}=L_f(\psi_{g,K})^{-1}\circ \psi_{f,\operatorname{CoCh}(g^*)K}^{-1}\circ Q_X(a_{K^\bullet})\circ\psi_{g\circ f,K}$. Its inverse is the descent of $a^{-1}$, since descent preserves identities and compositions.

source.place: Levelwise comparison and transport to derived categories; literature/blueprint/main-20261015/blueprint/sec-six-functors-basics/sk-prop-sfb-module-derived-factorization/sk-prop-sfb-module-derived-factorization.proof.md
source.note: The displayed component formula follows the localization node and the exact-functor comparisons.

proof.text:
Write $L_h^c$ for the restricted functors and $\iota_T:D_{\mathrm{cons}}(T,\Lambda)\hookrightarrow D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ for the inclusions. By [def-sfb-dc-upper-star], for $h:T\to S$ the restriction comes with its inclusion comparison $e_h:\iota_TL_h^c\xrightarrow{\sim}L_h\iota_S$ (an equality in the strict restriction model). Paste these comparisons with $c$ from step 2 to obtain
$$A:\iota_XL_{g\circ f}^c\xrightarrow{e_{g\circ f}}L_{g\circ f}\iota_Z\xrightarrow{c\iota_Z}L_fL_g\iota_Z\xrightarrow{L_fe_g^{-1}}L_f\iota_YL_g^c\xrightarrow{e_f^{-1}L_g^c}\iota_XL_f^cL_g^c.$$
Each arrow is a natural isomorphism, so their componentwise composite is one. All objects lie in the indicated domains because the restricted pullbacks of the cited definition are defined for every morphism of the setting and every commutative condensed $\Lambda$.

By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], morphisms between bounded constructible objects are exactly their ambient derived morphisms, with the same identities and composition. For each $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)$ define $c^c_K:L_{g\circ f}^cK\to L_f^cL_g^cK$ to be the morphism $A_K$, now read in this full subcategory; define its inverse to be $A_K^{-1}$ in the same way. The two inverse equations hold because their images are the ambient inverse equations and the Hom sets are unchanged. For every $u:K\to K\prime$, the naturality equation for these components is exactly the naturality equation for $A$ on $u$ in $D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Z,\Lambda)$, again in the same Hom set. Hence $c^c$ is a natural isomorphism and its image under $\iota_X$ is $A$.

If $b$ is another natural isomorphism with the specified ambient image, then for every $K$ its component $b_K$ and $c^c_K$ have the same image $A_K$. The inclusion is the identity on the Hom sets by [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], so $b_K=c^c_K$ for every $K$; componentwise equality gives $b=c^c$. Define the composition isomorphism to be $c^c$. Under the inclusion comparisons $e_h$ of step 3 its ambient image is $c$ of step 2, exactly as required.

lean.statement:
noncomputable def boundedConstructibleUpperStarComp {Z : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    [LocallyOfFiniteType Z.hom] [QuasiCompact Z.hom]
    [IsSeparated Z.hom] (g : Y ⟶ Z) :
    boundedConstructibleUpperStar Λ ℓ (f ≫ g) ≅
      boundedConstructibleUpperStar Λ ℓ g ⋙ boundedConstructibleUpperStar Λ ℓ f
lean.note: Exact existing match in the published WeilConjectures framework, read using scompile.py --source. The section parameters supply an arbitrary commutative condensed ring, a prime ell, a field of positive prime characteristic different from ell, separated finite-type objects X,Y,Z of Over (Spec k), and composable over-morphisms f,g. The definition lifts the ambient leftDerivedUpperStarComp through the fully faithful inclusion after pasting the three boundedConstructibleUpperStarCompatibility comparisons and associators. FullyFaithful.preimageIso gives precisely the ambient image, and faithfulness gives uniqueness. No finiteness-coefficient hypothesis is present. The branch records the published upstream source root with its live/side overlay, as for def-sfb-dc-upper-star. No new module or definition is introduced.
